content_html:
Nuvo is a free, open-source music player for Linux, Windows and macOS. It plays YouTube, SoundCloud and your own files, with synced lyrics, a ten-band equalizer and mixes made on your computer. Scene, its own visual engine, draws each song to the beat and turns any moment into a short video. You never make an account: your library, playlists and history stay on your machine.

nuvo.quest · Docs · Scene · Install · Why Nuvo · Roadmap

New in 0.4.0

  • Scene, Nuvo's own visual engine: each song draws itself to the beat and the words land as they are sung, with twelve ready scenes and a clip studio that exports MP4 up to 4K at 60 fps
  • Two editions with the same features: Standard by default, and Encrypted as a second download. Install the other one and your library converts on the next start
  • Moving sound: 4D, 8D and 16D circle the music around your head, in the new Space tab of the Sound panel
  • Lyrics follow the version that plays, and Find lyrics searches by title and artist in the lyrics editor
  • Notch placement: the screen, the side, the top edge, a gap and the stacking. On Hyprland and Sway it sits below your bar
  • Back always goes to the previous track, and a right click on a song on Home opens its menu
  • Home fills within seconds after your first picks, and the picker takes up to 15 songs and artists
  • Updates install when you quit, with a check every 4 hours and a Check for updates button
  • macOS gets the native window frame, the Notch over the menu bar and Discord status
  • Fixes for lyrics timing, imports, file names in old encodings, kaomoji on Linux and HDR on Hyprland

The full list is in the release notes.

See it

Search. Ctrl K opens one field for songs, artists and links, with YouTube and SoundCloud in one ranked list.

Karaoke. Lyrics light up word by word, in full screen or beside the player.

Wallpaper. A photo, a GIF or a video behind every screen, with the blur and fade you choose.

Queue. It opens beside whatever you are doing, with the history above.

Features

Scene

  • Twelve ready scenes, or your own from a background, up to three effects, a centrepiece and a text style
  • The stage runs on its own thread and its own clock, so a busy app never makes a lyric late
  • A clip studio with a timeline, a waveform and live frames: pick the moment, tune each part and see it at once
  • MP4 export in 9:16, 1:1 or 16:9, from 720p to 4K at 30 or 60 fps, the whole song or a cut, with fades. Your EQ, reverb and speed stay in the sound
  • Every exported frame carries a small "Made with Nuvo" mark

Search and play

  • One field for songs, artists and links, opened with Ctrl K
  • YouTube and SoundCloud results in one ranked list
  • Paste links from Apple Music, Deezer, Yandex Music, Shazam or TikTok, and share songs and playlists as compact links
  • Recognize a song from a video link, a file, the microphone or the sound your computer plays. The last two work on Linux

Library and mixes

  • Likes, saved albums and artists, playlists with custom covers, a duplicate finder
  • Playlists you can merge, sort six ways, keep offline, restore after a delete and pin
  • Mixes and radio from your plays and likes, "Not interested" with undo, a dislike button on every song
  • Statistics with a listening history that you can pause, export or delete
  • Tags, covers and .lrc files read from your folders

Sound

  • Gapless playback, crossfade of 1 to 12 seconds, queue, shuffle, repeat
  • Loudness normalization, speed and pitch with presets, reverb
  • Moving sound: 4D, 8D and 16D circle the music around your head, best on headphones
  • Sleep timer, A-B loop, moments to jump back to, trims for a song's start and end
  • Media keys, and MPRIS on Linux

Lyrics

  • Synced lyrics and karaoke by line, word, fill or step
  • Lyrics follow the version that plays, and Find lyrics searches by title and artist
  • Every word timed on your computer, and lyrics written for songs that have none. The models download once: 82 MB for timing, 264 MB for writing
  • Paste LRC or plain text and tap to sync, with a timing offset per track
  • Romanized lyrics for Korean, Chinese and Japanese kana, and translation through a local model

Imports

  • Playlist links from YouTube, SoundCloud, Apple Music, Deezer, Spotify and Yandex Music
  • Files: Spotify, Soundiiz, TuneMyMusic and Google Takeout exports, M3U, XSPF, CSV, TXT and Nuvo playlists
  • Save streamed tracks as files, original or MP3, and export playlists and the whole library

Your look

  • Nine themes, a colour editor with contrast checks, theme files, system or custom fonts
  • Custom CSS with a strict checker and a safe mode
  • The Notch, a small player at the top of the screen, on Windows, macOS, KDE, Hyprland, Sway and X11, on the screen, side and edge you pick. Off until you turn it on
  • A panel widget for the GNOME top bar, the Plasma panel and Waybar
  • Rebindable shortcuts, window zoom, a reduce-effects switch, English and Russian

Private by design

  • Two editions with the same features. Standard is the default; Encrypted encrypts the database and the audio cache, with a 24-word recovery phrase and an optional passphrase for the key
  • A local API on a private socket with a token per launch
  • HTTP and SOCKS5 proxies with a login, and a connection check for each service
  • Last.fm scrobbling with your own API key, off until you turn it on
  • A Discord status with the song cover. On by default; turn it off in Settings, Integrations, Discord
  • The update check contacts github.com. On by default; turn it off in Settings, Application, About

Why Nuvo

Each point links its sources, read on 2026-11-14, and says so when another player matches it.

  • Free, all of it. Every feature, no plan to pick. Nuvo Plus costs nothing, since it does not exist. Liner Plus costs $4 a month, and Mpthree Plus costs 149 ₽ per 30 days and holds Mpthree's equalizer, effects, crossfade, shortcuts and song recognition. Riff is free too. Liner pricing · Mpthree plans · Riff FAQ
  • The source is right here. AGPL-3.0-or-later: read it, build it, fork it and share your fork. Liner's licence forbids public forks and any build that talks to a server other than Liner's. Mpthree publishes no source. Riff is open as well, under MIT. Liner licence · Mpthree terms, 2.1 · Riff licence
  • No account, no Nuvo server. Your library lives in one file on your machine, so you have no password to forget. Liner keeps your library, playlists and plays on its server under your account, and Mpthree needs an account for Plus. Riff skips the account too. Liner privacy · Mpthree terms, 7.3 · Riff FAQ
  • Encrypted, with a way back in. The Encrypted edition encrypts your library and its audio cache. If the system keyring goes missing, your 24-word recovery phrase opens it. We found no encrypted library or recovery phrase on the official pages of Liner, Riff or Mpthree. Liner privacy · Liner storage · Riff README · Mpthree terms
  • The whole sound kit, free. A ten-band equalizer with twelve presets, speed, pitch and reverb, crossfade, gapless playback and loudness normalization. Mpthree sells its equalizer, speed, reverb and crossfade as Plus. Riff gives you an equalizer, speed, pitch and reverb at no cost. Mpthree terms, 2.3 · Riff README
  • Name that song. Nuvo recognizes a song from a file, a link, your microphone or what your computer plays (the last two on Linux), and keeps a history. Mpthree puts recognition in Plus. Liner and Riff do not document it. Mpthree terms, 2.3 · Liner site · Riff site
  • Lyrics for songs that have none. Nuvo listens to the track and times every word on your computer. Liner, Riff and Mpthree describe online lyrics, LRC files and manual offsets. Nuvo 0.3.0 · Liner site · Riff README · Mpthree site
  • Bring your library as a file. Exports from Soundiiz, TuneMyMusic and Google Takeout, Spotify CSV, XSPF and plain text, plus links from Spotify, Apple Music, Deezer, SoundCloud and Yandex Music. Riff takes links, Yandex Music among them, and its own JSON file. Liner takes links. Nuvo 0.3.0 · Riff site · Liner privacy
  • Statistics that stay yours. A story of your listening, charts, top lists and drill-downs, which you can export, delete or pause. Liner sends play events to its server for history and recommendations. Liner privacy
  • A proxy built in. SOCKS5 with a login and a connection check for each service, so you see which one your network blocks. Liner's FAQ points you to a VPN. Liner FAQ
  • arm64 for Linux and Windows. Liner 0.2.11, Riff 0.7.5 and Mpthree 1.1.0 list no arm64 build for either system. Pear Desktop does ship them. Liner 0.2.11 · Riff 0.7.5 · Mpthree downloads · Pear Desktop 3.12.0
  • Small tools. Moments to mark a spot and jump back, an A-B loop, trims for a song's start and end, romanized lyrics, a dislike button on every song and a reason beside each recommendation.

Install

Get the files from the latest release.

  • Linux: AppImage, .deb or .rpm, for x64 and arm64. The Encrypted edition keeps its key in a Secret Service keyring such as GNOME Keyring or KWallet. Without one, the key stays in a file that you can seal with a passphrase in Settings, Application, Storage. On a Chromebook, turn on Linux in the ChromeOS settings and install the .deb.
  • Windows: The installer (.exe) or the portable .zip, for x64 and arm64.
  • macOS: The .dmg for Apple silicon or Intel.

Nuvo Encrypted is the same app with the library and the audio cache encrypted on disk, under a key kept in your system keyring. Its files in the same release start with Nuvo-Encrypted-. Install either edition over the other and your library converts on the next start.

Each release lists SHA-256 checksums. Full steps and building from source are in the install guide.

If your system warns you the first time

Builds are not signed with a paid certificate yet. A certificate costs money every year and Nuvo is free, so your system may warn you the first time:

  • Windows: in SmartScreen, choose More info, then Run anyway.
  • macOS: open Nuvo once. When macOS blocks it, go to System Settings, Privacy & Security, and press Open Anyway.
  • Linux: make the AppImage executable and run it.

Roadmap

  • Planned: search by a lyric line, a music map and a year recap, genre and mood mixes, signed Windows and macOS builds.
  • Weighing: device sync with no Nuvo account, self-hosted music servers, plugins, a phone remote and a command line, room correction, per-device output routing.
  • Never: a Nuvo account or server, hosting or selling music, telemetry.

This is a direction, not a schedule. Details are in the roadmap.

content_html_zh:
Nuvo is a free, open-source music player for Linux, Windows and macOS. It plays YouTube, SoundCloud and your own files, with synced lyrics, a ten-band equalizer and mixes made on your computer. Scene, its own visual engine, draws each song to the beat and turns any moment into a short video. You never make an account: your library, playlists and history stay on your machine.

nuvo.quest · Docs · Scene · Install · Why Nuvo · Roadmap

New in 0.4.0

  • Scene, Nuvo's own visual engine: each song draws itself to the beat and the words land as they are sung, with twelve ready scenes and a clip studio that exports MP4 up to 4K at 60 fps
  • Two editions with the same features: Standard by default, and Encrypted as a second download. Install the other one and your library converts on the next start
  • Moving sound: 4D, 8D and 16D circle the music around your head, in the new Space tab of the Sound panel
  • Lyrics follow the version that plays, and Find lyrics searches by title and artist in the lyrics editor
  • Notch placement: the screen, the side, the top edge, a gap and the stacking. On Hyprland and Sway it sits below your bar
  • Back always goes to the previous track, and a right click on a song on Home opens its menu
  • Home fills within seconds after your first picks, and the picker takes up to 15 songs and artists
  • Updates install when you quit, with a check every 4 hours and a Check for updates button
  • macOS gets the native window frame, the Notch over the menu bar and Discord status
  • Fixes for lyrics timing, imports, file names in old encodings, kaomoji on Linux and HDR on Hyprland

The full list is in the release notes.

See it

搜索。 Ctrl K opens one field for songs, artists and links, with YouTube and SoundCloud in one ranked list.

Karaoke. Lyrics light up word by word, in full screen or beside the player.

Wallpaper. A photo, a GIF or a video behind every screen, with the blur and fade you choose.

Queue. It opens beside whatever you are doing, with the history above.

特征

Scene

  • Twelve ready scenes, or your own from a background, up to three effects, a centrepiece and a text style
  • The stage runs on its own thread and its own clock, so a busy app never makes a lyric late
  • A clip studio with a timeline, a waveform and live frames: pick the moment, tune each part and see it at once
  • MP4 export in 9:16, 1:1 or 16:9, from 720p to 4K at 30 or 60 fps, the whole song or a cut, with fades. Your EQ, reverb and speed stay in the sound
  • Every exported frame carries a small "Made with Nuvo" mark

Search and play

  • One field for songs, artists and links, opened with Ctrl K
  • YouTube and SoundCloud results in one ranked list
  • Paste links from Apple Music, Deezer, Yandex Music, Shazam or TikTok, and share songs and playlists as compact links
  • Recognize a song from a video link, a file, the microphone or the sound your computer plays. The last two work on Linux

Library and mixes

  • Likes, saved albums and artists, playlists with custom covers, a duplicate finder
  • Playlists you can merge, sort six ways, keep offline, restore after a delete and pin
  • Mixes and radio from your plays and likes, "Not interested" with undo, a dislike button on every song
  • Statistics with a listening history that you can pause, export or delete
  • Tags, covers and .lrc files read from your folders

Sound

  • Gapless playback, crossfade of 1 to 12 seconds, queue, shuffle, repeat
  • Loudness normalization, speed and pitch with presets, reverb
  • Moving sound: 4D, 8D and 16D circle the music around your head, best on headphones
  • Sleep timer, A-B loop, moments to jump back to, trims for a song's start and end
  • Media keys, and MPRIS on Linux

Lyrics

  • Synced lyrics and karaoke by line, word, fill or step
  • Lyrics follow the version that plays, and Find lyrics searches by title and artist
  • Every word timed on your computer, and lyrics written for songs that have none. The models download once: 82 MB for timing, 264 MB for writing
  • Paste LRC or plain text and tap to sync, with a timing offset per track
  • Romanized lyrics for Korean, Chinese and Japanese kana, and translation through a local model

Imports

  • Playlist links from YouTube, SoundCloud, Apple Music, Deezer, Spotify and Yandex Music
  • Files: Spotify, Soundiiz, TuneMyMusic and Google Takeout exports, M3U, XSPF, CSV, TXT and Nuvo playlists
  • Save streamed tracks as files, original or MP3, and export playlists and the whole library

Your look

  • Nine themes, a colour editor with contrast checks, theme files, system or custom fonts
  • Custom CSS with a strict checker and a safe mode
  • The Notch, a small player at the top of the screen, on Windows, macOS, KDE, Hyprland, Sway and X11, on the screen, side and edge you pick. Off until you turn it on
  • A panel widget for the GNOME top bar, the Plasma panel and Waybar
  • Rebindable shortcuts, window zoom, a reduce-effects switch, English and Russian

私人设计

  • Two editions with the same features. Standard is the default; Encrypted encrypts the database and the audio cache, with a 24-word recovery phrase and an optional passphrase for the key
  • A local API on a private socket with a token per launch
  • HTTP and SOCKS5 proxies with a login, and a connection check for each service
  • Last.fm scrobbling with your own API key, off until you turn it on
  • A Discord status with the song cover. On by default; turn it off in Settings, Integrations, Discord
  • The update check contacts github.com. On by default; turn it off in Settings, Application, About

Why Nuvo

Each point links its sources, read on 2026-11-14, and says so when another player matches it.

  • Free, all of it. Every feature, no plan to pick. Nuvo Plus costs nothing, since it does not exist. Liner Plus costs $4 a month, and Mpthree Plus costs 149 ₽ per 30 days and holds Mpthree's equalizer, effects, crossfade, shortcuts and song recognition. Riff is free too. Liner pricing · Mpthree plans · Riff FAQ
  • The source is right here. AGPL-3.0-or-later: read it, build it, fork it and share your fork. Liner's licence forbids public forks and any build that talks to a server other than Liner's. Mpthree publishes no source. Riff is open as well, under MIT. Liner licence · Mpthree terms, 2.1 · Riff licence
  • No account, no Nuvo server. Your library lives in one file on your machine, so you have no password to forget. Liner keeps your library, playlists and plays on its server under your account, and Mpthree needs an account for Plus. Riff skips the account too. Liner privacy · Mpthree terms, 7.3 · Riff FAQ
  • Encrypted, with a way back in. The Encrypted edition encrypts your library and its audio cache. If the system keyring goes missing, your 24-word recovery phrase opens it. We found no encrypted library or recovery phrase on the official pages of Liner, Riff or Mpthree. Liner privacy · Liner storage · Riff README · Mpthree terms
  • The whole sound kit, free. A ten-band equalizer with twelve presets, speed, pitch and reverb, crossfade, gapless playback and loudness normalization. Mpthree sells its equalizer, speed, reverb and crossfade as Plus. Riff gives you an equalizer, speed, pitch and reverb at no cost. Mpthree terms, 2.3 · Riff README
  • Name that song. Nuvo recognizes a song from a file, a link, your microphone or what your computer plays (the last two on Linux), and keeps a history. Mpthree puts recognition in Plus. Liner and Riff do not document it. Mpthree terms, 2.3 · Liner site · Riff site
  • Lyrics for songs that have none. Nuvo listens to the track and times every word on your computer. Liner, Riff and Mpthree describe online lyrics, LRC files and manual offsets. Nuvo 0.3.0 · Liner site · Riff README · Mpthree site
  • Bring your library as a file. Exports from Soundiiz, TuneMyMusic and Google Takeout, Spotify CSV, XSPF and plain text, plus links from Spotify, Apple Music, Deezer, SoundCloud and Yandex Music. Riff takes links, Yandex Music among them, and its own JSON file. Liner takes links. Nuvo 0.3.0 · Riff site · Liner privacy
  • Statistics that stay yours. A story of your listening, charts, top lists and drill-downs, which you can export, delete or pause. Liner sends play events to its server for history and recommendations. Liner privacy
  • A proxy built in. SOCKS5 with a login and a connection check for each service, so you see which one your network blocks. Liner's FAQ points you to a VPN. Liner FAQ
  • arm64 for Linux and Windows. Liner 0.2.11, Riff 0.7.5 and Mpthree 1.1.0 list no arm64 build for either system. Pear Desktop does ship them. Liner 0.2.11 · Riff 0.7.5 · Mpthree downloads · Pear Desktop 3.12.0
  • Small tools. Moments to mark a spot and jump back, an A-B loop, trims for a song's start and end, romanized lyrics, a dislike button on every song and a reason beside each recommendation.

安装

Get the files from the latest release.

  • Linux: AppImage, .deb or .rpm, for x64 and arm64. The Encrypted edition keeps its key in a Secret Service keyring such as GNOME Keyring or KWallet. Without one, the key stays in a file that you can seal with a passphrase in Settings, Application, Storage. On a Chromebook, turn on Linux in the ChromeOS settings and install the .deb.
  • Windows: The installer (.exe) or the portable .zip, for x64 and arm64.
  • macOS: The .dmg for Apple silicon or Intel.

Nuvo Encrypted is the same app with the library and the audio cache encrypted on disk, under a key kept in your system keyring. Its files in the same release start with Nuvo-Encrypted-. Install either edition over the other and your library converts on the next start.

Each release lists SHA-256 checksums. Full steps and building from source are in the install guide.

If your system warns you the first time

Builds are not signed with a paid certificate yet. A certificate costs money every year and Nuvo is free, so your system may warn you the first time:

  • Windows: in SmartScreen, choose More info, then Run anyway.
  • macOS: open Nuvo once. When macOS blocks it, go to System Settings, Privacy & Security, and press Open Anyway.
  • Linux: make the AppImage executable and run it.
